newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Foreigners still far below Taiwan stock ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners still far below Taiwan stock ceiling.

text.p: Foreign investors have remitted US$10.625 billion into Taiwan's stock market, leaving room for US$71.83 billion more before hitting the official ceiling, the central bank said on Wednesday.
Foreign investors may invest up to $82.455 billion in the stock market under rules capping foreign holdings at 25 percent of the bourse's market value, the bank said in a statement.
In September 1996, the bank raised the ceiling to 25 percent from 20 percent and allowed foreign individuals to trade Taiwan stocks.
In January, foreign funds remitted into the stock market totalled US$736.472 million, up from US$552.897 million in December 1996, the statement said.
A total of US$441.441 million of such funds flowed out of Taiwan in January, down from December's US$643.190 million.
Aside from direct stock market holdings, the bank has allowed inflow of a total of $1.66 billion for funds raised overseas by local firms through convertible bonds and global depositary receipts.
In this category, foreigners as of February 5 had remitted US$355 million into Taiwan and could send US$1.305 billion more before reaching a legal ceiling, the bank said.
